# dotnet-inspect

CLI tool for inspecting .NET libraries and NuGet packages. It is for .NET what `docker inspect` and `kubectl describe` are for container land.

It operates on three types of content:

- **Platform libraries** — e.g., `System.Collections` (shipped with the .NET SDK)
- **NuGet packages** — e.g., `Microsoft.Extensions.AI`
- **Local paths** — e.g., `path/to/library.dll` or `path/to/package.nupkg`

```bash
dotnet-inspect Microsoft.Extensions.AI              # Bare name — routes to best source
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json             # Package metadata
dotnet-inspect library System.Text.Json             # Library metadata
dotnet-inspect type --package System.Text.Json      # Discover types (terse)
dotnet-inspect member JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json  # Inspect members (docs)
dotnet-inspect find "Chat*,Diction*"                # Search types across scopes
dotnet-inspect diff System.Text.Json@9.0.0..10.0.2  # API version comparison
dotnet-inspect extensions HttpClient                # Extension methods
dotnet-inspect implements Stream                    # Interface implementers
dotnet-inspect depends 'INumber<TSelf>'              # Type dependency hierarchy
dotnet-inspect samples Markout MarkoutWriter        # Code samples
dotnet-inspect demo list                            # Curated showcase queries
dotnet-inspect cli                                  # CLI args explorer
```

## Bare Names

A bare name like `dotnet-inspect System.Text.Json` uses a router to pick the best asset. Platform libraries like `System.Text.Json` and `Microsoft.AspNetCore` ship in both the platform and as NuGet packages. The tool assigns a **platform orientation** to `System.*` and `Microsoft.*` names that are found in downloaded ref/runtime packs. Other names (e.g., `Microsoft.Extensions.AI`, `Newtonsoft.Json`) route to NuGet packages.

To override routing, use explicit commands: `package System.Text.Json` or `library --package System.Text.Json`.

## Commands

### package

Inspect NuGet packages — metadata, files, versions, dependencies.

```bash
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json                     # Metadata (latest version)
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json 8.0.0               # Specific version (positional)
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json@8.0.0               # Specific version (@ syntax)
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json --version 8.0.0     # Specific version (flag)
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json -v:d                # Detailed — dependencies, stats
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json -v:q                # Quiet — compact line
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json@8.0.0 -s "Vulnerabilities"  # Select section
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json --tfm net8.0 -v:d   # Filter to TFM
```

Package data:

```bash
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json --versions          # List available versions
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json --version           # Show latest version
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json --version 11.0.0-preview*  # Wildcard version
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json --files             # File listing
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json --tfms              # TFM list
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json --layout            # Tree view of files
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json --layout --lib      # Tree view filtered to lib/
dotnet-inspect package dotnet-inspect --layout --tools      # Tree view for tool packages
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json --dependencies      # Package dependency tree
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json --tfm net9.0 --dependencies  # Dependencies for specific TFM
```

Custom NuGet sources:

```bash
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json --version 11.0.0-preview* \
  --add-source https://dnceng.pkgs.visualstudio.com/public/_packaging/dotnet11/nuget/v3/index.json --prerelease
dotnet-inspect package MyPackage --source https://my-feed/v3/index.json
dotnet-inspect package MyPackage --nugetconfig ./nuget.config
```

Package search (NuGet discovery):

```bash
dotnet-inspect package search "Azure.AI"               # Search NuGet by keyword
dotnet-inspect package search "AWSSDK" --take 20       # Limit results
dotnet-inspect package search "Aspire" --json          # JSON output
```

### library

Inspect a library — metadata, symbols, references, dependencies, resources.

```bash
dotnet-inspect library System.Text.Json                     # Platform library (runtime)
dotnet-inspect library --package System.Text.Json            # Library from NuGet package
dotnet-inspect library --package System.Text.Json -v:q       # Compact line
dotnet-inspect library ./bin/MyLib.dll                       # Local file
```

Library sections (13 total):

```bash
dotnet-inspect library --package System.Text.Json -s        # List sections
# Library Info, Symbols, Source Link Audit, Library References, Library References (Transitive),
# Dependencies, Extension Methods, Unsafe Methods, P/Invoke Methods, Resources,
# Custom Attributes, Type Forwarders, Non-normalized Paths
```

Key features:

```bash
dotnet-inspect library System.Text.Json --references -s Lib*         # Direct references
dotnet-inspect library Microsoft.Extensions.AI.OpenAI --dependencies # Dependency tree (visual)
dotnet-inspect library --package System.Text.Json --source-link-audit  # SourceLink audit
dotnet-inspect library --package System.Text.Json --extract-resources resources/  # Extract resources
dotnet-inspect library --package System.Text.Json -s Resour*         # View embedded resources
```

### type

Discover types in a package or library — terse output, no docs by default.

```bash
dotnet-inspect type --package System.Text.Json                   # All types (from package)
dotnet-inspect type --platform System.Text.Json                  # All types (from platform)
dotnet-inspect type System.Text.Json                             # Bare name — auto-routes
dotnet-inspect type -t "JsonS*" --package System.Text.Json       # Types matching glob
dotnet-inspect type JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json --shape  # Type shape diagram
dotnet-inspect type 'HashSet<T>' --platform System.Collections --shape  # Generic types (quote!)
dotnet-inspect type --package System.Text.Json --oneline         # Columnar output
dotnet-inspect type --package System.Text.Json --json            # JSON output
```

### member

Inspect type members — docs on by default, supports dotted syntax.

```bash
dotnet-inspect member JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json         # All members (docs on)
dotnet-inspect member JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json --no-docs  # Suppress docs
dotnet-inspect member JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json -m Serialize  # Filter to member
dotnet-inspect member JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json -m 'Deseri*'  # Glob member filter
dotnet-inspect member -m JsonSerializer.Deserialize --package System.Text.Json  # Dotted syntax
dotnet-inspect member 'Option<T>' --package System.CommandLine          # Generic types (quote!)
```

Section filtering:

```bash
dotnet-inspect member JsonArray --package System.Text.Json -v:d -s:Interfaces  # Interfaces only
dotnet-inspect member JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json -s:Methods    # Methods only
```

Member selection and decompilation — use `--select` to see `Name:N` addressing hints, then drill in:

```bash
$ dotnet-inspect member OptionsFactory --package Microsoft.Extensions.Options --select
## Constructors

| Select | Name | Signature |
| ------ | ---- | --------- |
| `.ctor:1` | .ctor | `void .ctor(IEnumerable<IConfigureOptions<TOptions>>, ...)` |
| `.ctor:2` | .ctor | `void .ctor(IEnumerable<IConfigureOptions<TOptions>>, ..., IEnumerable<IValidateOptions<TOptions>>)` |

## Methods

| Select | Name | Signature |
| ------ | ---- | --------- |
| `Create:1` | Create | `TOptions Create(string)` |
```

Then target a member using the `Name:N` shorthand to get source, decompiled C#, and IL:

```bash
$ dotnet-inspect member OptionsFactory --package Microsoft.Extensions.Options Create:1
## Source                          # Original C# (via SourceLink)
## Lowered C#                     # Decompiled C# faithful to IL semantics
## IL                             # Raw IL disassembly with resolved tokens
## IL (Annotated)                 # IL with pre-execution stack state at each instruction
```

For constructors with overloads, `--params` can also disambiguate:

```bash
dotnet-inspect member OptionsFactory --package Microsoft.Extensions.Options \
  -m .ctor --params "IEnumerable<...>,IEnumerable<...>"           # Overload by params
```

Other flags:

```bash
dotnet-inspect member JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json --oneline  # One member per line
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine --ctor          # Constructor details
dotnet-inspect member JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json --json     # JSON output
```

### api (deprecated)

The `api` command is deprecated. Use `type` for type discovery or `member` for member inspection.

### find

Search for types across packages, frameworks, and local assets.

```bash
dotnet-inspect find HttpClient                           # Search default scope (curated)
dotnet-inspect find "*Stream*" -n 10                     # Glob pattern, limit results
dotnet-inspect find "*Json*" --package System.Text.Json  # Search in package
dotnet-inspect find "*Serializer*" --package System.Text.Json --package Newtonsoft.Json  # Multiple packages
dotnet-inspect find ILogger --aspnetcore                 # ASP.NET Core packages
dotnet-inspect find "ChatClient*" --oneline                # Search default scope, columnar output
dotnet-inspect find "*Logger*" --platform                # All platform frameworks
dotnet-inspect find "*Host*" --extensions                # Microsoft.Extensions packages
dotnet-inspect find "*Command*" --project ./MyApp.csproj # Project dependencies
dotnet-inspect find "*Service*" --bin ./bin/Debug/net8.0  # Built output directory
```

Batch search (comma-separated patterns):

```bash
dotnet-inspect find "Chat*,Diction*" -v:q
dotnet-inspect find "Option*,Argument*,Command*" --package System.CommandLine --oneline
```

| Scope | Description |
| ----- | ----------- |
| (none) | Default scope (all platform frameworks + Microsoft.Extensions.AI) |
| `--platform` | All platform frameworks (runtime, aspnetcore, netstandard) |
| `--extensions` | Curated Microsoft.Extensions.* packages |
| `--aspnetcore` | Curated Microsoft.AspNetCore.* packages |
| `--package` | NuGet package (name or name@version). Repeatable. |
| `--package-prefix` | All packages matching a NuGet ID prefix (e.g., `Azure.AI`). Resolves via search. |
| `--library` | Local library file |
| `--project` | Project dependencies via project.assets.json |
| `--bin` | All DLLs in output directory |

Scope flags are combinable: `--platform --package Newtonsoft.Json` searches both.

| Option | Description |
| ------ | ----------- |
| `--oneline` | One result per line, columnar output |
| `--no-header` | Suppress column headers (use with --oneline) |
| `-n` | Limit results per pattern |

### diff

Compare API surfaces between versions. Changes are classified as breaking, additive, or potentially breaking.

```bash
dotnet-inspect diff System.CommandLine@2.0.0-beta4.22272.1..2.0.3 -v:q  # Full package diff
dotnet-inspect diff JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json@9.0.0..10.0.2  # Single type
dotnet-inspect diff "*Writer*" --package Markout@0.1.8..0.2.0            # Glob filter
dotnet-inspect diff JsonSerializer --platform System.Text.Json@8.0.23..10.0.2  # Platform versions
dotnet-inspect diff System.Text.Json@9.0.0..10.0.2 --oneline             # One change per line
dotnet-inspect diff System.Text.Json@9.0.0..10.0.2 --breaking           # Breaking only
dotnet-inspect diff System.Text.Json@9.0.0..10.0.2 --additive           # Additive only
dotnet-inspect diff System.Text.Json@9.0.0..10.0.2 --name-only          # Type names only
```

### extensions

Find extension methods/properties for a type. Detects both classic extension methods and C# 14 extension properties.

```bash
dotnet-inspect extensions HttpClient                                 # Default curated scope
dotnet-inspect extensions HttpClient --reachable                     # Include reachable types
dotnet-inspect extensions HttpClient --platform                      # All platform frameworks
dotnet-inspect extensions DbContext                                  # Default scope
dotnet-inspect extensions IServiceCollection \
  --package Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection \
  --package Microsoft.Extensions.Azure                               # Multi-package scan
dotnet-inspect extensions IDistributedApplicationBuilder \
  --package Aspire.Hosting --package Aspire.Hosting.Redis \
  --package Aspire.Hosting.PostgreSQL --tfm net8.0                   # Aspire builder extensions
```

The `--reachable` flag finds extensions on types accessible via properties and methods (e.g., `HttpClient` → `HttpResponseMessage` → `.Content` → `HttpContent`).

### implements

Find types implementing an interface or extending a base class.

```bash
dotnet-inspect implements Stream                                     # Default scope
dotnet-inspect implements Stream --platform                          # All platform frameworks
dotnet-inspect implements IDisposable --extensions                   # Microsoft.Extensions packages
dotnet-inspect implements IJsonTypeInfoResolver --package System.Text.Json  # In package
```

### depends

Walk the type dependency hierarchy upward — the inverse of `implements`. Shows what interfaces a type implements or extends, recursively expanding each into its own dependencies.

```bash
dotnet-inspect depends 'INumber<TSelf>'                                  # Interface hierarchy
dotnet-inspect depends 'IFloatingPointIeee754<TSelf>'                    # Deeper hierarchy
dotnet-inspect depends Int128                                            # Concrete type's full graph
dotnet-inspect depends Stream                                            # Base class hierarchy
```

### demo

Run curated showcase queries that exercise the tool's capabilities. Each demo prints the equivalent CLI invocation so users can repeat and modify it.

```bash
dotnet-inspect demo                                  # Random pick ("I'm feeling lucky")
dotnet-inspect demo list                             # List all available demos
dotnet-inspect demo 1                                # Run a specific demo by index
dotnet-inspect demo --feeling-lucky                  # Random pick (explicit flag)
```

### samples

Fetch and display code samples for a type from SourceLink-indexed sources.

```bash
dotnet-inspect samples Markout MarkoutWriter --list  # List available samples
dotnet-inspect samples Markout MarkoutWriter         # Print all samples
dotnet-inspect samples Newtonsoft.Json JObject        # Third-party examples
```

Also accessible via `member` command: `dotnet-inspect member Markout MarkoutWriter --samples -v:q`

### cache

Manage the dotnet-inspect cache (downloaded ref packs, packages, sources, symbols).

```bash
dotnet-inspect cache                                # Show cache size breakdown
dotnet-inspect cache --clean                        # Clear the cache
```

### cli

CLI args explorer — tree view of command structure.

```bash
dotnet-inspect cli                                  # Tree view (single level)
dotnet-inspect cli -v:d                             # Deep view (all levels)
dotnet-inspect cli -v:q                             # Command names only (oneliner)
dotnet-inspect cli type                             # Explore args for specific command
```

## Output Control

### Verbosity

| Flag | Level | Output |
| ---- | ----- | ------ |
| `-v:q` | Quiet | Title + compact summary line |
| `-v:m` | Minimal | + description (default) |
| `-v:n` | Normal | + metadata table, type parameters |
| `-v:d` | Detailed | + all sections, full signatures |

Every verbosity level includes a **compact summary line**:

```text
Version: 8.0.0 | Type: Library | TFM: net8.0 | Updated: 2023-11-14 | Vulnerabilities: 2
```

### Section Filtering

```bash
dotnet-inspect library --package System.Text.Json -s              # List available sections
dotnet-inspect library --package System.Text.Json -s Exten*       # Glob matching
dotnet-inspect System.Text.Json -v:d -s "Extension Methods"       # Include by name
dotnet-inspect System.Text.Json -v:d -x:Statistics,Files          # Exclude by name
```

### JSON

```bash
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json --json                    # Full JSON
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json --json --compact          # Minified, nulls omitted
dotnet-inspect library Aspire.Hosting -s Ext* --json | jq '...'   # Pipe to jq
```

### Tips

Contextual suggestions written to `stderr`:

```bash
dotnet-inspect -T:d                  # More tips
dotnet-inspect -T                    # Silence tips (defaults to -T:q)
dotnet-inspect -v:q                  # Also silences tips
DOTNET_INSPECT_TIPS=quiet            # ENV-based silencing
```

## Key Options Reference

| Option | Description | Commands |
| ------ | ----------- | -------- |
| `--package` | NuGet package source | type, member, library, find, extensions, implements, depends, diff |
| `--package-prefix` | All packages matching NuGet ID prefix | find, extensions, implements |
| `--platform` | Platform library source (string) / all platform frameworks (bool) | type, member, library, diff (string) / find, extensions, implements, depends (bool) |
| `--extensions` | Curated Microsoft.Extensions.* packages | find, extensions, implements, depends |
| `--aspnetcore` | Curated Microsoft.AspNetCore.* packages | find, extensions, implements, depends |
| `--library` | Local library file | type, member, find, extensions, implements |
| `--tfm net8.0` | Select target framework | package, library, type, member, extensions |
| `-t Pattern` | Filter types by glob pattern | type |
| `-m Name` | Filter to member (supports globs, Type.Member syntax) | member |
| `--shape` | Type shape diagram (hierarchy + members) | type |
| `--select` | Show Select column with Name:N shorthand | member |
| `--index N` | Target Nth overload (or use Name:N shorthand) | member |
| `--params "..."` | Target overload by parameter types | member |
| `--docs` | Include XML documentation (on by default for member) | member |
| `--no-docs` | Suppress XML documentation | member |
| `--samples` | Fetch code samples | member |
| `--ctor` | Constructor details | member |
| `--oneline` | One result per line, columnar | type, member, find, diff, implements |
| `--dependencies` | Dependency tree (visual) | library, package |
| `--references` | Direct assembly references | library |
| `--source-link-audit` | SourceLink/determinism audit | library |
| `--extract-resources dir/` | Extract embedded resources | library |
| `--versions` | List available versions | package |
| `--version` | Show latest version (or specify version) | package |
| `--files` | List files | package |
| `--tfms` | List target frameworks | package |
| `--layout` | File tree view | package |
| `--reachable` | Include reachable type extensions | extensions |
| `--no-header` | Suppress column headers | type, member, find, diff, implements |
| `--breaking` | Breaking changes only | diff |
| `--additive` | Additive changes only | diff |
| `--name-only` | Names only | diff |
| `-n N` | Limit results | find, extensions, package |
| `--all` | Include hidden/obsolete | implements, find |
| `--json` | JSON output | all commands |
| `-v:q/m/n/d` | Verbosity | all commands |
| `-s Name` | Include section (glob-capable) | all commands |
| `-x Name` | Exclude section | all commands |
| `-T:q/d` | Tips verbosity | all commands |
| `--prerelease` | Include prerelease versions | package --versions |
| `--add-source URL` | Add NuGet source | package |
| `--source URL` | Use specific NuGet source | package |

## LLM Usage Guide

### Prefer --oneline for Discovery

Use `--oneline` as the default format for scanning APIs. It is far more token-efficient than the default markdown tables, shows overload counts in the DETAIL column, and includes constructors that may be missing from other views for generic types.

```bash
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine --oneline       # scan all members
dotnet-inspect type --package System.CommandLine --oneline                  # scan all types
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine -m SetAction -v:d  # then drill in
```

Only switch to `-v:d` when you need full signatures, docs, or source for a specific member.

### Migration Workflow (fixing build errors from API changes)

When code fails to compile because it uses an outdated API:

```bash
# 1. Identify the version gap (check .csproj PackageReference versions)
# 2. Diff the old and new versions to see all breaking/additive changes
dotnet-inspect diff --package System.CommandLine@2.0.0-beta4.22272.1..2.0.2

# 3. Scan the new type surface with --oneline
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine@2.0.2 --oneline

# 4. Enumerate overloads for a method (--select shows Name:N indices)
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine@2.0.2 --select

# 5. Drill into a specific overload by index
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine@2.0.2 -m SetAction:1
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine@2.0.2 -m SetAction:3  # async overload
```

Start with `diff` — it immediately shows all removed/changed/added members. This avoids guessing which APIs changed.

**Verbosity tip:** Default verbosity is usually sufficient for migration. Use `-v:d` only when you need source code or IL — it shows one overload at a time and generates much more output. Use `--select` or overload index (`SetAction:2`) to see all overloads efficiently.

### Important: New type and member Commands

The `api` command is deprecated. Use `type` for discovery and `member` for inspection:

```bash
# Type discovery (terse, no docs)
dotnet-inspect type --package System.Text.Json                  # All types
dotnet-inspect type -t "*Serializer*" --package System.Text.Json  # Filter by glob

# Member inspection (docs on by default)
dotnet-inspect member JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json   # All members
dotnet-inspect member JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json -m Serialize  # Filter to member
dotnet-inspect member -m JsonSerializer.Deserialize --package System.Text.Json  # Dotted syntax
```

### Common Mistakes to Avoid

```bash
# WRONG: Using -v:d for initial scanning (wastes tokens)
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine -v:d              # ✗
# CORRECT: Use --oneline for scanning, -v:d only for specific members
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine --oneline         # ✓
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine -m SetAction -v:d # ✓ (drill in)

# WRONG: Using -v:d to see all overloads (only shows one at a time)
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine -m SetAction -v:d # ✗ (shows first overload only)
# CORRECT: Use --select to see overload indices, then drill into specific ones
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine --select          # ✓ (shows Name:N for each)
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine -m SetAction:3    # ✓ (async overload)

# WRONG: Not using diff when fixing API migration errors
# CORRECT: Start with diff to see all changes at once
dotnet-inspect diff --package System.CommandLine@2.0.0-beta4.22272.1..2.0.2 # ✓

# WRONG: Using --filter to filter members (doesn't exist)
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine --filter .ctor    # ✗
# CORRECT: Use -m flag or positional arg for member filtering
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine -m SetAction      # ✓
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine .ctor             # ✓ (constructors)

# WRONG: Using empty angle brackets for generic types (resolves to abstract base)
dotnet-inspect member "Option<>" --package System.CommandLine                # ✗ (shows Option, not Option<T>)
# CORRECT: Use <T> to get the concrete generic type with constructors
dotnet-inspect member 'Option<T>' --package System.CommandLine               # ✓ (shows Option<T> with .ctor)

# WRONG: Expecting RootCommand to show inherited members from Command
dotnet-inspect member RootCommand --package System.CommandLine               # only shows RootCommand's own members
# WORKAROUND: Also query the base type to see inherited methods like Add() and SetAction()
dotnet-inspect member Command --package System.CommandLine --oneline         # shows Add(), SetAction(), Parse()

# WRONG: --platform on search commands doesn't take a library name (it's a bool flag)
dotnet-inspect find "IHost*" --platform Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting   # ✗
# CORRECT: Use --package for specific NuGet packages, --extensions for curated set
dotnet-inspect find "IHost*" --package Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting    # ✓
dotnet-inspect find "IHost*" --extensions                              # ✓ (curated set)

# WRONG: Two separate version args for diff
dotnet-inspect diff System.Text.Json@8.0.0 System.Text.Json@9.0.0     # ✗
# CORRECT: Single arg with .. range separator
dotnet-inspect diff System.Text.Json@8.0.0..9.0.0                     # ✓

# WRONG: Running --help to learn syntax (wastes tokens)
dotnet-inspect type --help                                              # ✗
# CORRECT: Use llmstxt for complete syntax reference
dotnet-inspect llmstxt                                                 # ✓

# WRONG: Using -m without the type name
dotnet-inspect member --package Newtonsoft.Json -m SerializeObject     # ✗
# CORRECT: Provide type as positional arg, or use dotted syntax
dotnet-inspect member JsonConvert --package Newtonsoft.Json -m SerializeObject  # ✓
dotnet-inspect member -m JsonConvert.SerializeObject --package Newtonsoft.Json  # ✓
```

### Scope Flags on Search Commands (find, extensions, implements, depends)

- **`--platform`** (bool): All platform frameworks (runtime, aspnetcore, netstandard ref packs).
- **`--extensions`**: Curated Microsoft.Extensions.* packages (DI, Logging, Configuration, etc.).
- **`--aspnetcore`**: Curated Microsoft.AspNetCore.* packages (Authentication, Mvc, SignalR, etc.).
- **(no flags)**: Default scope — all platform frameworks + Microsoft.Extensions.AI.
- **`--package`**: Specific NuGet packages. Combinable with scope flags.

Note: `type`, `member`, `library`, `diff` still use `--platform <name>` as a string option for specific platform libraries.

- **Bare names**: The tool auto-routes. `System.Text.Json` → platform; `Newtonsoft.Json` → package.

### Generic Type Syntax

Use C# generic syntax — the tool auto-converts to metadata format:
- `"List<T>"` → `List\`1`
- `"Dictionary<TKey, TValue>"` → `Dictionary\`2`

Quote the type name to prevent shell interpretation: `'Option<T>'`

**Important:** Use `<T>` (not `<>`) to target the concrete generic type. `"Option<>"` resolves to the abstract base `Option`, which hides constructors and generic-specific members. `"Option<T>"` resolves to the actual `Option<T>` class with its constructor and `DefaultValueFactory` property.

### Method Signatures

Signatures include `params` and default values from metadata:

```text
void .ctor(string name, params string[] aliases)
ParseResult Parse(Command command, IReadOnlyList<string> args, ParserConfiguration? configuration = null)
```

### Common Library Names

| Types | Platform Library |
| ----- | ---------------- |
| List, Dictionary, Queue, HashSet | System.Collections |
| String, Int32, Object, Span | System.Runtime |
| JsonSerializer, JsonDocument | System.Text.Json |
| HttpClient, HttpRequestMessage | System.Net.Http |
| Regex, Match | System.Text.RegularExpressions |
| Task, ValueTask | System.Threading.Tasks |
| File, Stream, Path | System.IO |

### Discovery Workflow

```bash
# Step 1: Find the type
dotnet-inspect find "JsonSerializer"
# Shows: System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer in System.Text.Json.dll

# Step 2: Scan the type surface (--oneline for efficiency)
dotnet-inspect type JsonSerializer --platform System.Text.Json --oneline

# Step 3: Get type shape
dotnet-inspect type JsonSerializer --platform System.Text.Json --shape

# Step 4: Scan members (--oneline shows overload counts in DETAIL column)
dotnet-inspect member JsonSerializer --platform System.Text.Json --oneline

# Step 5: Drill into specific members when you need full signatures
dotnet-inspect member JsonSerializer --platform System.Text.Json -m Serialize -v:d

# Step 6: View decompiled source for a specific overload
dotnet-inspect member JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json Serialize:1

# Or use dotted syntax (no type positional needed)
dotnet-inspect member -m JsonSerializer.Serialize --package System.Text.Json
```
